Sports.title: Arsenal’s midfield depth signals ominous warning to title rivals – and Maresca’s City | Ed Aarons
Sports.content:
If this was a glimpse of the Premier League’s new order then the rest had better watch out. By the time Martin Ødegaard sat Gianluigi Donnarumma down to make it 3-0 to the champions, the Arsenal party was in full swing. “Can we play you every week?” their supporters gleefully taunted their counterparts in sky blue.

Those in red and white who had made the journey to south Wales could barely believe what they were watching, even if winning the Community Shield is unlikely to spark the same kind of celebrations that were seen on the streets of north London in May after ending a 22-year wait to win the title. Having been forced to settle for three successive second-place finishes before finally reaching the summit, this time it was Manchester City’s fans who had to face the reality of being humbled by their closest rivals. As Viktor Gyökeres had put it beforehand: “Against City? In a friendly? We want to win.” That much was clear from the opening whistle at the Principality Stadium.

It was fitting that the first match of the post-Pep Guardiola era should pit two of his former assistants and pretenders to his crown against each other. On this evidence Mikel Arteta’s powerful Arsenal squad, which looks deeper than this time last year after the additions of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis, will head into the new season as clear favourites to defend their crown after blowing away Enzo Maresca’s City in the space of 48 minutes.

The Italian had barely taken his seat in the dugout for his first meaningful match since replacing Guardiola when his new side found themselves trailing. Myles Lewis-Skelly was a major factor in Arsenal finally getting over the line in May after being brought into the midfield engine room for the run-in when Martín Zubimendi had run out of gas. The teenager needed little more than 20 seconds to remind Thomas Tuchel what England were missing this summer with his brilliant pass for Riccardo Calafiori’s opener.

Lewis-Skelly doesn’t turn 20 until next month but already looks a match physically for most – including City’s £116m new signing, Elliot Anderson. Lewis-Skelly’s future has been the subject of speculation this week, with reports that he had been offered to Manchester United and Chelsea. But after dominating Anderson and the veteran Mateo Kovacic in partnership with the outstanding Guimarães, Arteta will surely not allow him to depart in the next fortnight.

As for Guimarães, one typically aggressive challenge from the Brazil midfielder to dispossess Phil Foden was all it took for Arsenal’s supporters to fall in love. The chants of “Bruno, Bruno” only amplified when he sprayed a crossfield pass perfectly into the path of Noni Madueke and City will have been relieved to see the back of him at half-time.

View image in fullscreen Martin Ødegaard’s return as an attacking force is yet another reason for Arsenal to feel optimistic. Photograph: Charlotte Wilson/Offside/Getty Images

By then, Kai Havertz had already made it 2-0 after a beautifully crafted goal involving Ødegaard and Tzolis, and City were hanging on for dear life. Seeing Declan Rice emerge for the second half was another reminder of Arsenal’s plethora of options, although the wisdom of Bukayo Saka returning so soon after England’s World Cup exploits remains to be seen in the long term. “He said it’s not done,” sang the Arsenal fans in reference to Rice’s post-match team talk at the Etihad Stadium after they were beaten in March, when he was introduced.

The re-emergence of Ødegaard as an attacking force is yet another reason for Arsenal to feel optimistic. The captain’s campaign was severely hampered by injury last season but, after excelling for Norway at the World Cup, he was at the heart of Arsenal’s best moves and capped an excellent performance with a cool finish to round off the scoring. That was also greeted with chants of “you’re getting sacked in the morning” directed towards Maresca, who was seen deep in conversation with his players and staff at the full-time whistle.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

With Rodri set to depart for Barcelona, recruiting at least one more central midfielder to partner Anderson must be a priority. Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi would provide youthful energy, although given Arsenal’s strength in that department more experience will be required if they are going to mount a serious title challenge. Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández may fit the bill.

There was a brief moment last autumn when Maresca’s former side looked most capable of challenging Arsenal before his squabbles with the hierarchy brought an end to the Italian’s tenure. It will take some time to make his imprint on a squad that was so heavily devoted to Guardiola, although Arteta said this week that he believes his newest rival has “the personality, the character and, especially, the knowledge” to be successful. For the Arsenal manager, the question is now whether he can build a legacy that could one day rival Guardiola’s. This was a good way to start.

Sports.title: Rodri set to complete Barcelona move after Manchester City accept £65.4m bid
Sports.content:
Rodri looks set to complete a move to Barcelona after Manchester City accepted a bid of £65.4m from the Spanish club.

The 30-year-old World Cup winner had entered the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium and made it clear he would like the opportunity to move to Barcelona. City, who are now closing in on a deal to sign Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, were reluctant sellers but had little choice with the Spanish international out of contract next summer.

City had already rejected Barcelona’s bid of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri last week after an initial offer of €45m (£38.5m) but have now accepted the latest bid.

Speaking after City’s 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal on Sunday, Enzo Maresca called Rodri a “top player” and said “all the teams need Rodri”, but City have been unable to persuade their linchpin to stay and sign a new contract. Rodri had only returned to the club on Friday, having undergone back surgery after the World Cup, with Maresca saying he had given him a “big hug” when he first met up with him.

Rodri has spent seven seasons with City, winning the Premier League four times and scoring the only goal when they beat Inter in the 2023 Champions League final. The following year he won the Ballon d’Or but, by the time he was presented with the trophy, he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament which ruled him out of most of the 2024-25 campaign, while hamstring and groin problems limited him to 33 appearances in Pep Guardiola’s final campaign in charge.

City have already undergone major changes in midfield this summer, spending £116m on Elliot Anderson, while agreeing a deal to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah. They are now ready to seal a move for the Morocco star Bouaddi.

The teenager impressed at the World Cup and Lille had initially wanted any potential move to include a 12-month loan deal back to the French side. However, with City losing Bernardo Silva and now Rodri, Maresca is keen to bulk up his midfield options for the new campaign and want Bouaddi available for this season. City have also been linked with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández and retain an interest.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 11: Hull City
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 20th (NB: this is not necessarily Louise Taylor’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 6th (Championship)

Prospects

It is no exaggeration to say that Hull’s playoff triumph in May was a shock. They had, after all, started the season as Championship relegation favourites and operated under a transfer embargo throughout the campaign. Moreover, they conceded 66 league goals, the fourth-highest, along the way. Now another minor miracle will surely be required if Premier League survival is to be secured.

Much may hinge on Oli McBurnie, the scorer of 19 goals last season, succeeding where he has struggled in the past and retaining his scoring touch in the top tier, but there is no lack of optimism in East Yorkshire. “Think about us like a volcano,” says Hull’s owner, Acun Ilicali. “It’s boiling right now and it’s going to erupt.”

Hull intend following Sunderland’s template last summer by making 14 new signings, albeit on a significantly smaller budget. So far 11 – Jack Butland, Hidemasa Morita, Matt Targett, Óscar Zambrano, Jens Hjertø-Dahl, Elliot Stroud, Konstantinos Tzolakis, Lucas Herrington, Joe Gelhardt, Lucas Gourna-Douath and the club record buy, the central defender Nobel Mendy, who has arrived from Rayo Vallecano for just over £20m – have arrived.

“The transfer market is very slow,” said the manager, Sergej Jakirovic, who covets the Sunderland striker Wilson Isidor and last season’s 23-goal Championship top scorer, Swansea’s Zan Vipotnik. “But, in the last seven days of the window, it will become very, very quick.”

His cause has been hindered by pre-season injuries, with perhaps the biggest blow involving an arm problem suffered by Butland. It threatens to keep the former Rangers goalkeeper, who had impressed in friendlies, out until Christmas. The consensus is that Hull will have long since become a lost cause by then, but, much as the impressive Jakirovic needs new faces and Premier League nous, he does hold one ace card. Hull boast an exceptionally powerful team spirit driven by exemplary on-field leaders, including the veteran central defender John Egan. Maybe, just maybe, it can, once again, transport them further than anyone believes possible.

Off-field picture

In June, the playoff winners faced kicking off the new Premier League season handicapped by a near certain six-point deduction. A club that spent last season under a two-window English Football League transfer embargo avoided it by selling their goalkeeper Ivor Pandur and midfielder Aidon Shehu to Rangers and Panathinaikos respectively for a combined £8.5m. Access to the fruits of the top tier’s broadcast deal has since made Hull a whole lot wealthier, but Ilicali has pledged not to risk the club’s future by overspending and, at the time of writing, has invested around £78m on the new players.

Owner-fan relationship

Unpredictable and slightly conflicted. Ilicali, the Turkish sports reporter turned media mogul – who is on his fifth manager since taking control in early 2022 – was offered a wholesale welcome when he took over from the unpopular Allam family, but he now exerts much more of a polarising effect on supporters. If November 2022, when he treated 320 fans to an all-expenses-paid week’s holiday at a luxury resort hotel in Antalya represented a high point, a nadir arrived when late payments resulted in Hull being placed under a transfer embargo last season. Nonetheless, the playoff triumph ensures many are prepared to offer the 57-year-old the benefit of the doubt.

The manager

The Mostar-born, 49-year-old Jakirovic has Bosnian and Croatian citizenship and says his life was shaped by the 1990s Balkan war that broke out when he was 14. “It was life or death,” he has said. “It has made me the person I am today.” Shortly after his arrival from Turkey’s Kayserispor, in June 2025, Hull were placed under a transfer embargo, but, defying widespread predictions of imminent relegation, he led the team to sixth place before beating Middlesbrough in the Championship playoff final. A central midfielder or central defender in his playing days, the former Bosnia and Herzegovina international led Dinamo Zagreb to the Croatian League and Cup double in 2024.

Star signing

View image in fullscreen Hidemasa Morita applauds the Sporting fans during the Portuguese Cup final in May, his last appearance for the Lisbon club. Photograph: SPP Sport Press Photo/Alamy

The Japan defensive midfielder Hidemasa Morita joined from Sporting Lisbon after four trophy-laden years in Portugal. A fans’ favourite in Lisbon, he played regular Champions League football last season as Sporting reached the quarter-finals and has 40 senior international caps. Morita could have stayed in Lisbon, but opted not to renew his contract in order to experience Premier League football. Hull fended off competition from Ipswich for the signature of the 31-year-old who was a key part of the Japan squad at Qatar 2022. Morita is the second Japanese player to represent Hull and his amalgam of experience and quality in a key position promise to prove invaluable.

Stat attack

The strangest part of the Championship playoffs might not have been the Southampton spying scandal. Hull were second-bottom for expected points, 53.1, and would have been relegated if underlying performances determined results. It was remarkable tthey won promotion and it will be even more surprising if they make a serious fist of staying up.

Set for a breakthrough

The 22-year-old central defender Charlie Hughes was Hull’s young player of the year last season and his assurance in possession and excellent passing range are bound to catch all sorts of Premier League eyes. Helpfully, his ballplaying ability is matched by some equally impressive – and combative – defending. After spending his youth in the academies of Liverpool and Manchester City, Hughes joined Wigan, leaving for Hull last summer. An imposing blend of steel and silk, a defender also comfortable in central midfield will miss the start of the season after hernia surgery. Happily, Hughes is expected back by early autumn at the latest and appears integral to the team’s survival hopes.

World Cup impact

Not content with helping Hull win the most unexpected of promotions, the Canada winger Liam Millar headed across the Atlantic to the World Cup. He made three appearances at the tournament as they reached the knockout stage, losing to Morocco in the round of 16. Given his career seemed in real jeopardy when he suffered a serious knee injury shortly after joining Hull in 2024, inclusion in Canada’s squad represented the fulfilment of an unlikely looking dream. “It was an unbelievable experience,” said the 26-year-old. “I’ve never seen Canada the way it was, I’ve never seen so many red shirts in Vancouver and Toronto. We want to inspire the next generation and I think we did Canada proud.”

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Manchester City to move for Alexis Mac Allister?
Sports.content:
After looking a tad silly in the Community Shield loss to Arsenal, with not having a midfield being one problem for Enzo Maresca and the further blow of Rodri’s departure getting closer, Manchester City really need some new blood. A surprise name linked to them is Alexis Mac Allister of Liverpool, who may receive a bid in the coming days as City aim to ready themselves for the Premier League season.

Ibrahim Mbaye has been linked with every club around, so it should come as no shock that Manchester United have held talks over signing the Paris Saint-Germain winger, who was left out of the matchday squad for the French Super Cup on Sunday.

There will be a bit of movement in and out of the defence at Leeds, with Nico Elvedi joining fromBorussia Mönchengladbach, while Sebastiaan Bornauw heads to Hamburg on loan. Another player departing Elland Road is the goalkeeper Lucas Perri who has agreed to sign for Torino on an initial loan with the option to stay un Italy permanently.

West Ham had earmarked Troy Parrott as a potential striking option but AZ Alkmaar are not too keen on selling the Republic of Ireland international for less than £21m. Nuno Espírito Santo is having to look elsewhere and Joel Piroe of Leeds has crept up the shortlist. The Hammers looked blunt in front of goal on Sunday against Burnley so may be required to pay up. Leeds would like the forward to go permanently but could accept a loan if push comes to shove.

Coventry are targeting goals: with Taiwo Awoniyi signed up, they are set to complete a move for Fenerbahçe striker Sidiki Cherif for £20.5m. The talented teenager started his career with Angers before heading to Turkey on loan. He only signed permanently this summer but Fener are happy to make a quick profit. Frank Lampard may return to former club Chelsea to bolster his defensive ranks by acquiring Josh Acheampong, with the Sky Blues contemplating a temporary or permanent move for the full-back.

Chelsea need to clear a few fringe players from the books over the next fortnight. Another person potentially not of use to Xabi Alonso is the centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo, who is wanted by Marseille. Benfica have also made an enquiry.

Ethan Nwaneri’s absence from the Arsenal squad in Cardiff on Sunday was duly noted. Milan are favourites to give the midfielder a new home. The 19-year-old did not pull up any trees during a loan spell with Marseille but his creative talents may be better suited abroad, it would seem. One man heading out of Milan is Christopher Nkunku. He is not wanted at the San Siro, which could open the door for Newcastle to snap him up. The Premier League side could face competition from Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig.

Sports.title: Brighton’s Emilie Joramo: ‘I feel like I’m now in the place I want to be’
Sports.content:
Emilie Joramo has long had her sights set on the Women’s Super League, but she held herself back from pushing for a move over from Scandinavia – until now.

“I’d been interested in the league for a long time now and it was a goal for me to get here one day,” says Joramo, who Brighton signed on a free transfer at the end of June. “It was about finding the right path for me to get here. I didn’t want to go too early, I wanted to feel ready for it both physically and mentally. Now, everything just felt right.”

Brighton had been tracking the Norwegian midfielder for some time and the 24-year-old was aware of their interest. An encouraging conversation with Brighton’s manager, Dario Vidosic, and good meetings with the club as her contract with Hammarby drew closer to its end meant she was at last ready to join the league she had followed from afar.

That time in Sweden with Hammarby, with whom she reached the Europa Cup final last season, and before that in her homeland with Rosenborg who she helped win the Norwegian Cup for the first time in 21 years, was crucial in preparing her for her latest challenge.

“I had so much fun at Hammarby and I’ve got so many good friends there,” she says. “I grew both as a football player and as a person in those years. I didn’t feel ready when I was 21, when I went to Sweden, to come over here. I felt like I needed to play a bit more, to play every game, that was really important for me.”

That Brighton had been aware of her for some time was a boost too. “It’s reassuring for me that they really wanted me,” she says. “They hadn’t just watched a couple games, they’d been following me for years, and that’s really important to me because I’m not going to jump at the first opportunity I get. I like to think things through and it has to feel right for me.”

View image in fullscreen Emilie Joramo played Champions League qualifying last year, and helped Hammarby reach the final of the inaugural Europa Cup Photograph: Emma Wallskog/Bildbyrån/Shutterstock

For Brighton fans wondering what they are getting, there should be some excitement too. Joramo is fiercely motivated and feels she fits the possession-based style of football that Vidosic wants his team to play.

“I would say that I’m a hardworking player,” she says, when asked to describe herself. “I always give 100% all of the time. I can’t do 50, 60, 70, I’m always 100%. I want to have the ball. I want to play, not just put balls in behind but to keep the ball , play with each other, [build] good relationships with the other players and think several steps ahead. They’ve always been things that I’m good at and I’m always wanting to get better at too.”

Brighton and the WSL present a step up. “I think I can get challenged a lot here because things go much faster, the intensity is higher, you have a smaller amount of time when you have the ball,” she says. “So, it’s a perfect place for me to be at now to be challenged further and develop my strengths but also the parts that I’m not as strong at and need to develop more.”

Arriving and starting life on the south coast was “a bit overwhelming” in the beginning: “There’s so many people to get to know, the staff is so much bigger than what I’ve been used to. So, instead of one physio you have five and you need to get to know everyone and get to know which person does which role. That’s always the way it is in a new team, of course, but it’s much bigger here.”

Everyone has been very welcoming and her first impressions of training sessions under Vidosic have been positive. “I’ve only had two sessions with him so far,” she says, “but he seems very, very good at football tactics, how the game works, how to play good football, and that was important for me because I’m a player that wants to have the ball and always wants to try to get better and try to play good football together as a team, not only as individuals. This is what Dario wants, so it really fits my ambitions, my values and how I want to play.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Emilie Joramo was Brighton’s second signing of the summer window – they have since added five more. Photograph: James Boardman/Brighton and Hove Albion

She is finding her feet on the pitch, and starting to find them off it. Joramo’s girlfriend has moved to England with her, which has helped the transition and helps her escape football when needed. “I have to have other things to do besides football,” she says. “We’ve been to the beach and have been exploring the city. It’s so different for me to live by the beach, I’m from the mountains and the woods. This is like a holiday for me, and with the weather as well, it’s been so warm. It’s really nice.”

The goal now is “to contribute as much as I can to this team and play as much as I can”, but Joramo’s patience as she worked towards her WSL goal should continue to serve her well. “I feel like I’m now in the place I want to be and develop in and I need to give it a bit of time in the beginning, because I can be very impatient,” she says. “I have to give it some time to get into it, get into the intensity and everything around the game here, because it’s so much more than what I’m used to in Sweden, this is so much bigger.”

At the end of her first season in England is a big carrot, should Norway come through a two-legged playoff against Romania and then another against Albania or Wales and qualify for the 2027 Women’s World Cup.

Joramo made her debut for the senior side in 2022 and has been on the fringes of the squad since, making three appearances in total and playing for the under-23s. In April she was on the bench for the senior side’s back-to-back qualification campaign wins over Slovenia and she is hopeful her WSL move helps her show what she can bring.

“Hopefully this also will strengthen my opportunities with the national team,” she says. “I know this is the best league in the world, so if I get to play here, then I’ve done something right, I think.”

Sports.title: Flemming’s dramatic Burnley double pegs back West Ham on Championship return
Sports.content:
There are many good reasons why Burnley and West Ham are performing as Premier League tribute acts, slumming it in the Championship with the hope of a shot at the limelight once more. They are two flawed teams, relegated because of chronic defects, and plenty were on show as West Ham blew a two-goal lead to start life on the second-tier circuit with an entertaining draw.

Zian Flemming’s late double secured a thoroughly deserved point for the hosts, who showed promise going forward but took far too long to find a clinical finish. Despite going two goals ahead through Maximilian Kilman and Manor Solomon, West Ham rarely looked comfortable as they sat back, something that eventually cost them.

“We did a very good first half,” Nuno Espírito Santo said. “We created a lot of situations we were able to control and stop Burnley. Not so good in the second half, but after we scored the second goal, I think we should have done better to keep the result.”

Nuno continued his career-long love of conservatism and his side were put under pressure early on, only surviving through Burnley’s poor decision-making and inept finishing. In addition to continuity in the dugout, West Ham can boast their captain, Jarrod Bowen, who committed to the club rather than seek a quick return to the top flight this summer. It was his corner that found Kilman at the back post after he lost Aaron Ramsey in the box.

Considering West Ham are favourites to go back up, this fortuitous lead should have been a foundation to build on, but little attempt was made to seek a second. They were passive for long periods, composed in possession, but Burnley were able to counter at speed through the midfield and cause problems, only to lack the composure to make the most of those situations.

Nuno tried to rectify the faltering midfield by sending on James Ward-Prowse for the anonymous Pablo, a player who has yet to find his level in England. It made no difference as Burnley came out the better side, pinning West Ham back repeatedly, but Flemming appeared destined to not score, finding the fans, goalkeeper, the inside of the post and Ollie Scarles on the line rather than the back of the net.

West Ham reminded everyone that they possess Premier League quality as Mohamadou Kanté made light work of Marcus Edwards on the right wing before pulling the ball back to Solomon to slam home from close range. This was their second and final shot on target, both leading to goals. Despite being second best, the visitors must have believed they were out of sight, by accident rather than design.

View image in fullscreen Maximilian Kilman gives West Ham the lead as he heads home Jarrod Bowen’s cross. Photograph: COLORSPORT/Alan Martin/Shutterstock

Flemming had other ideas as things finally clicked, aided by Scarles crudely taking out Edwards in the box, allowing the striker to settle his nerves after 83 minutes of near misses and create tension in the West Ham ranks. It worked as the visitors failed to clear a corner which Flemming swept home in the second minute of added time, further explaining why he has attracted transfer interest. Asked if Flemming will stay the Burnley manager, Nicky Hayen, who is desperate not to lose his talisman, said: “It does not help that he scored twice today.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Nuno will want more action in the transfer market after the record Championship signing of Arne Engels from Celtic on Saturday. A striker is much needed as Taty Castellanos made little impact, while the aforementioned Pablo does not give the impression of a man who will fire West Ham to promotion. The bench featured five academy graduates, none of who Nuno felt comfortable bringing on, which says a lot. “The club knows the targets and the needs of the team. [We are] working very hard and trying to get the bodies in as soon as possible,” Nuno said. “We need especially in the offensive part of the team.”

Hayen, celebrating his 46th birthday, took his team on a lap of honour after his first league game in charge as he aims to build a relationship with supporters, who suffered through plenty of unwatchable football under his predecessor. “We showed resilience and that’s why I’m really satisfied for these boys because they worked really hard to change this game around and also how we did it,” Hayen said. “I’m pleased with the fans, how they supported us for 95 minutes. We invested a lot of time before this game into them because what we wanted was really to find the connection with them, that we made the promise that we bring energy into the stadium, that we keep on going for 95 minutes and this is exactly what we did.”

Sports.title: Scotland appoint Pocognoli as successor to Clarke in fresh approach
Sports.content:
The Scottish Football Association has appointed the Belgian Sébastien Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke as manager. The 39-year-old, who was sacked by Monaco in June, will become the country’s first non-Scottish manager since Berti Vogts, who was in charge from 2002 to 2004.

Clarke’s abrupt departure came after Scotland were knocked out of the World Cup at the group stage. He had signed a four-year contract extension immediately before the tournament. It quickly became clear the SFA would turn towards a foreign manager with the Danes Jon Dahl Tomasson and Kasper Hjulmand being linked with the position.

Pocognoli, a left-back who played for Brighton and West Brom, will probably be welcomed by Scotland fans seeking a fresh approach. Clarke was in position for a generally successful seven years, including appearances at three major tournaments, but was often criticised for a pragmatic style.

Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief football officer, said Pocognoli “will bring an aggressive, front-foot style of play that will excite supporters”.

After a period in youth coaching, Pocognoli enjoyed a successful time in charge of Union Saint-Gilloise in his homeland. Under Pocognoli, Union won their first title in 90 years in 2025. A move to Monaco followed, but Pocognoli lasted eight months and 38 games in France. The former Everton and Belgum winger Kevin Mirallas is expected to join him in the dugout.

Pocognoli said: “When I first heard of the interest, I was immediately excited about the opportunity. Scotland’s supporters are famous for their passion – most recently at the World Cup in the USA - and I have experienced it myself as a player for Belgium when we played in 2013.

“Along with my coaching staff, I will do everything I can to give them a team to be proud of and build on the success that has been achieved already by my predecessor.”

Scotland begin their Nations League campaign with a trip to Slovenia on 26 September. Pocognoli’s first home game in charge will be Switzerland’s visit to Glasgow three days later.

Sports.title: Nabizada stunner edges Watford past Southampton as ‘Spygate’ still looms large
Sports.content:
Southampton will have to get used to being barracked as they travel the Championship this autumn, the “Spygate” team set to be everyone’s favourite boo boys in the second tier. Certainly that was the case in Hertfordshire, with Watford fans and players alike beside themselves after a hard-fought victory, decided by two memorable first-half goals.

Tonda Eckert, the Southampton head coach, remains under investigation for his part in the Spygate affair and presented a subdued figure both during and after this contest. He insisted that his team were more united than ever after suffering the indignity of being removed from last season’s playoffs, “but it would be easier to say that after a victory”, Eckert acknowledged.

Watford paid tribute to Kenny Jackett before the match, the one-club legend and local boy hailed with two minutes of applause. This celebration of longevity and connection, with a Panini-inspired tifo tumbling down the stands, cut a contrast with the current operation, where Alessio Dionisi has become Watford’s 12th full-time manager in just the past five years.

“I am very tired and my team was too by the end,” said the Italian who was coaching Empoli in Serie B last season. Dionisi praised the attitude of his team – “I liked the mentality of my players, in every moment I saw one team working together,” he said. He also benefited from the Pozzo family’s multi-club network and the local academy in digging out a victory.

The Spain under-21 attacker Iker Bravo was one of several signings to make the familiar trek from “sister” club Udinese this summer, and he made his mark quickly, opening the scoring with a quite stunning solo goal in the 12th minute. It was all his own work and Bravo had to deploy a combination of skills to turn an innocuous situation into real danger. Looking to latch on to a long ball some 40 yards from goal, the 6ftplaymaker won the first header then, crucially, got a second touch with an outstretched toe to get the ball under control. Bravo then span immediately and drove at goal, pushing his way into the box before chopping right and getting off a low shot that Daniel Peretz got a hand to, butcould not keep out.

View image in fullscreen Watford’s Amin Nabizada jumps for joy after scoring their second goal against Southampton. Photograph: Peter Tarry/PA

A great way to start any season, the energy among the Vicarage Road crowd grew immediately and the home side went on to dominate the first half. They doubled their lead in the 29th minute with a moment to remember for 19-year-old academy graduate Amin Nabizada who exploited the same gaps on the left of the Southampton defence to run with the ball from his own half before finishing precisely from a tight angle. “Nabizada was emotional but after the first 10 minutes he played well,” Dionisi said. “When there is one mentality amongst the team, then it’s better for him too.”

Southampton had the better of the second half, taking advantage of a drop in tempo from the hosts to assert their interests. A spell of concerted possession in the 56th minute ended with Kuryu Matsuki pulling out wide, the young midfielder Cam Bragg moving unmarked into the half space and his shift left finding the Canada World Cup star Cyle Larin to poke home from 10 yards out.

Larin had a chance to equalise just two minutes later with a shot on the turn but Federico Ravaglia – another new signing to impress for the Hornets – turned the ball round the post. When Finn Azaz came on as a second-half substitute for the Saints he bought an inch to fire off a low drive that went just beyond the left hand post. As a succession of dangerous set pieces were sent over by Ryan Manning, Southampton fans were singing “we’ll score when we want”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

But as the game passed through a flurry of substitutions Eckert’s team were unable to generate enough momentum to truly unsettle Dionisi’s men. Their only further chance came in added time and was scuffed wide by Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

Eckert said he had been happy enough with his team’s performance beyond “two errors in possession”. He insisted his squad are “very close and united” as a group. “We had a different expectation for the result but the group looks united and we now need to turn that into results.”

Opening matches rarely offer much insight into how a season will pan out. But Watford fans were able to enjoy both temperate weather and a decent performance. If Southampton want to transform the negative energy of Spygate into something positive, meanwhile, they will have to start again next week.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy targeted by footballing giant as Premier League winner’s future takes surprise twist
Sports.content:
Jamie Vardy making a surprise move to Sao Paulo has not been totally ruled out.

Vardy, who is a free agent, is of interest to the Brazilian powerhouse.

3 Vardy is set for his third different club in as many seasons Credit: Getty

Alex Crook's on Jamie Vardy to Sao Paulo rumours

In response to the Sao Paulo whispers, Crook said on talkSPORT Breakfast: “That doesn't surprise me because Jamie Vardy still looks in top physical condition.

"He did pretty well over in Italy.

“I think he'd prefer a return to English football, but I wouldn't totally rule out a move to Brazil.

“Who knows, that might be the next chapter of the documentary that I've just started watching about his incredible career.

“But he's certainly got no shortage of interest. Sheffield Wednesday, his boyhood club, have chanced their arm. I think financially that's quite a difficult deal for the Owls to do.”

Which clubs are in for Jamie Vardy?

Owls chairman David Storch admitted live on talkSPORT's Weekend Breakfast show he'd be 'thrilled' to have Vardy at the club.

Storch added the club is 'trying to figure out' how to navigate around their financial restrictions in order to put a viable offer on the table for Vardy.

However, talkSPORT understands working within the imposed restrictions to make Vardy an attractive offer is viewed as extremely challenging.

The Owls and Sao Paulo are far from alone in the Vardy sweepstakes.

West Ham is another contender, having made an inquiry for the 39-year-old prior to the Championship campaign getting underway.

3 Vardy has been heavily linked with a return to English football Credit: Getty

Hammers boss Nuno Espirito Santo is keen on adding extra firepower to his attack, with the club also pursuing ex-Spurs striker Troy Parrott.

Leeds United forward Joel Piroe is another potential option on West Ham's striker shortlist.

Prior to the West Ham links, Vardy sent Leicester City fans into meltdown when he shared a video of himself training at the club during the off-season.

In the clip, Vardy even sported Leicester's training kit, sparking speculation he was in line for an emotional return to the club where he won the Premier League and scored 200 goals across all competitions.

However, Vardy was only back at his old stomping grounds simply to check his fitness levels.

When did Jamie Vardy become a free agent?

Vardy is available having departed Italian club Cremonese following their relegation from Serie A.

3 Vardy's Italian stint didn't quite go to plan Credit: Getty

The 39-year-old only signed a one-year deal with the team but was prepared to pen an extension had they stayed up.

But his seven goals and three assists in 29 appearances was ultimately not enough to help preserve Cremonese's Serie A status.

Sports.title: Premier League 2026/27 opening weekend fixtures, kick-off times and talkSPORT coverage in full
Sports.content:
The 2026/27 Premier League season is now just days away.

With the World Cup over, the top-flight is ready to return and the countdown is on for the opening game of the campaign.

4 Mikel Arteta's champions face Coventry on the first day of the new season Credit: Getty



And Coventry will get things underway with their first game back in the Premier League for 25 years, facing champions Arsenal.

All 380 games for the 2026/27 season were confirmed in June and also see newly-promoted Hull City hosting Michael Carrick's Manchester United on the opening weekend.

Liverpool, under new manager Andoni Iraola, travel to Newcastle with a fit-again Alexander Isak, who swapped the north east for the north west in a £125million transfer last summer.

Meanwhile, Tottenham travel to Brentford and feel they have the right manager in charge in Roberto De Zerbi, who guided them to safety on the final day of the 2025/26 season.



And Xabi Alonso's first game as Chelsea boss takes him to Fulham on Monday night, while it could be a changed Man City side that takes on Bournemouth with Elliot Anderson in the middle.

When does the Premier League season begin?

Arsenal, winners last season, begin the new season on Friday, August 21 as they take on Coventry at the Emirates at 8pm.



The top-flight opener will be exclusively live on talkSPORT.

Hull host Man United at 12:30pm on the first Saturday of the season - also on talkSPORT - while Brentford vs Tottenham is the 5:30pm match and there are a trio of 3pm games.

Newcastle vs Liverpool is the first 4:30pm Sunday match of the new campaign.



And Fulham vs Chelsea rounds off the opening weekend on Monday night, again live on talkSPORT.

Opening day fixtures Friday, August 21 Arsenal v Coventry City, 8pm - talkSPORT EXCLUSIVE Saturday, August 22 Hull vs Manchester United, 12:30pm - talkSPORT EXCLUSIVE

Everton vs Crystal Palace, 3pm

Ipswich vs Sunderland, 3pm

Nottingham Forest v Leeds United, 3pm

Brentford vs Tottenham, 5:30pm Sunday, August 23 Brighton vs Aston Villa, 2pm

Man City vs Bournemouth, 2pm

Newcastle vs Liverpool, 4:30pm Monday, August 24 Fulham vs Chelsea, 8pm - talkSPORT EXCLUSIVE

Who do the promoted clubs play?

Ipswich are back in the big time, having last played against West Ham in 2025 and losing 3-1.

Their first home game is against Sunderland and it will be new manager Gary O'Neil's opening competitive match in charge.

Hull, who were beaten by Tottenham 7-1 in their last Premier League game in 2017, won't have it easier against a revitalised United side led by Carrick, who was given the manager's role having guided them to third place last season.



"What a great game for us," Hull assistant manager Dean Holden told talkSPORT. "We had an incredible season last year to get promoted.

"I was sat doing an interview at a similar time last year talking about the Championship fixtures, and people were having us as one of the relegation favourites.

"So, what the club did to get promoted is nothing short of incredible. And to then see the fixtures come out this morning, it just all seems very real."

4 Hull City celebrate their return to the top tier by hosting Man United on the first Saturday game of the season, which is live on talkSPORT Credit: Getty



4 Lampard's Coventry go to Arsenal on the opening day and he hosts former club Chelsea in December Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Elsewhere, it has been a long time coming for Coventry, whose last Premier League game was in May 2001.

A trip to Arsenal first will delight manager Frank Lampard, who will relish the test of playing the champions.

Opening weekend live on talkSPORT

talkSPORT will be across all of the opening weekend's action with three games to be broadcast live on the station.



Our dedicated team will be at the Emirates as Arsenal kick off their title defence against Coventry.

Likewise, fans can catch all of the action from the MKM Stadium when newly-promoted Hull host United at Saturday lunchtime.

The weekend's exclusively live action on talkSPORT concludes with the west London derby between Fulham and Chelsea on Monday evening at 8pm.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.



Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

4 Xabi Alonso makes the short trip to Fulham for his first Premier League match as Chelsea boss Credit: Getty



Boxing Day is back!

The Premier League has addressed the packed festive schedule over the Christmas and New Year period with no two match rounds taking place within 60 hours of each other.

Fans will be delighted to know that the traditional Boxing Day schedule will return to its usual slot on December 26.

Just one Premier League fixture took place on Boxing Day last season sparking major backlash from fans.

But there will be no such controversy this time around with multiple games expected to be televised on the day, pending broadcasting picks.



Arsenal face a festive trip to the the scene of their title celebrations when they face Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park.

Newcastle United host Manchester City, Nottingham Forest travel to Old Trafford to take on Manchester United and Hull entertain Liverpool.

Elsewhere, Tottenham take on Bournemouth, Frank Lampard faces an emotional reunion with former club Chelsea at the CBS Arena and Aston Villa host Leeds.

Sports.title: Serie A forward rushed to intensive care as club release statement
Sports.content:
Cagliari have confirmed striker Yael Trepy is in intensive care.

The club added Trepy is receiving treatment at the Santissima Annunziata Civil Hospital in Sassari.

2 Trepy has been with Cagliari since 2022 Credit: Getty

Cagliari issue statement on Yael Trepy

"The club is in constant contact with the healthcare facility and the player's family and is closely monitoring the progress of his condition," a club statement read.

"At this time, Cagliari Calcio's thoughts are with Yael and his family.

"The club also requests that their privacy be respected and will provide any updates as they become available."

News of Trepy's hospitalisation comes just days after he started Cagliari's Coppa Italia clash against Arezzo.

Trepy logged 54 minutes for Cagliari as they progressed into the second round of the competition with a 1-0 victory last Friday.

Who is Yael Trepy?

The 20-year-old, who joined Cagliari's youth ranks in 2022 from French side US Creteil-Lusitanos, has nine appearances for the club's first team.

Trepy scored on his Serie A debut last term, rescuing a 2-2 draw against Cremonese with a goal in the 88th minute.

He went on to feature an additional seven times in the Italian top flight, all of which were appearances off the bench.

The majority of the French forward's appearances last season were made in Primavera 1, the top division of youth football in Italy.

Trepy featured 24 times for Cagliari Primavera last term, netting 11 times.

2 The forward has 33 goals for Cagliari across all of their youth and senior teams Credit: Getty

He finished as the team's second-top scorer in the competition, with Senegalese forward Paul Mendy scoring 14 goals.

Despite the duo's goals, Cagliari finished 18th in Primavera 1, meaning they were forced to play Napoli in a relegation play-off where the loser would drop down a division.

Luckily for Cagliari, a 3-0 win over Napoli preserved their Primavera 1 status.

The Sardinian club begins their Serie A campaign on Saturday when they travel to face Parma.

Sports.title: Juventus to sign Premier League goalkeeper after Emiliano Martinez transfer collapses
Sports.content:
Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario is set to join Juventus on an initial loan move, talkSPORT understands.

The Old Lady have accelerated a move to bring the Italy international back to Serie A after withdrawing their interest in Aston Villa's Emiliano Martinez.

3 Juve are set to bring in Vicario from Tottenham on a loan with buy option deal Credit: Getty

Vicario had been regarded as a viable option for Juventus in their quest to sign a new number one between the sticks.

The 29-year-old has been expected to depart north London this window having lost his starting spot to Antonin Kinsky at the end of last season.

Kinsky came into the team after Vicario was forced to undergo hernia surgery in March, with the Czech Republic international starting the final seven Premier League matches.

Despite being fit for the final two games as Spurs battled relegation, boss Roberto De Zerbi opted to stick with Kinsky.

Vicario had been linked with a move to join Serie A champions Inter Milan after agreeing personal terms.

But Inter instead opted to bring in Ivan Provedel from Lazio - opening the door for Juventus to be given a free run.

And they have had a loan bid with an option to buy clause - believed to be worth around £8.5million - accepted by Tottenham.

Why did Juventus pull out of a deal to sign Martinez?

It had been thought that Martinez would join Juventus, with the ex-Arsenal man telling Villa that he wanted to leave and join the two-time Champions League winners in June.

We told you on Sunday how Juve had submitted an £8.5m offer for the 2022 World Cup winner.

The Turin giants launched an initial £6m bid with £2.5m to be paid in potential add-ons.

3 Vicario is on his way out of Spurs after joining from Empoli in 2023 Credit: Getty

However, with Villa demanding an £8.5m flat fee, Juve ultimately decided to not proceed with another offer.

Juventus had concerns over Martinez's broken finger, which he sustained in the warm-up of Villa's eventual Europa League final win over Freiburg in May.

Martinez revealed last month that he had been playing through the pain barrier while on World Cup duty with Argentina.

He said: "It still hurts every day, I knew it was going to hurt a lot. I avoided surgery.

"All the specialists I consulted told me I had to have surgery or I wouldn't be able to play."

He added: "Throughout the entire group stage I couldn't train with the group and it affected me because it's something I love.

3 Martinez will not be joining Juventus from Aston Villa - despite being the subject of a bid Credit: Getty

"Afterwards, from Egypt onward, I trained normally and I feel much better.

"Up until two days before the first match [3-0 win over Algeria], I was playing with one hand, I looked like I had one arm.

"Now, continuing and talking to people, it's all in my head. It doesn't affect me at all."

Martinez now faces an uncertain future at Villa Park with Unai Emery's side close to bringing in Parma star Zion Suzuki, with talkSPORT exclusively informing you of a possible deal on Saturday.
